## ✨ Highlights

A kernel built for what Janus runs on - KVM/QEMU virtual machines - and
a Controller that keeps offering updates when GitHub's downloads falter.

- 🐧 **A kernel for virtual machines**: both kernel tracks drop the
  drivers no KVM/QEMU guest has - physical network cards, NVMe, RAID
  controllers, USB... The kernel is a quarter smaller, and 14 to 20 %
  fewer of the kernel's published vulnerabilities apply to it.
- 🖥️ **Updates stay visible through GitHub's hiccups**: a release whose
  files GitHub answers with errors for a while is still offered.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Janus runs on KVM/QEMU virtual machines only** (Proxmox, libvirt,
  the Controller's machines): the kernel drives virtio disks and
  network cards, SATA/IDE and SCSI disks, and the Intel e1000/e1000e
  cards QEMU emulates. It has no driver for physical machines' NVMe
  disks, RAID controllers or network cards, nor for VMware's - bare
  metal and VMware were already suspended targets, and come back with
  a kernel of their own once someone tests them
  ([what Janus supports](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/README.md#what-janus-supports),
  [physical hardware](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/provisioning-a-node.md#physical-hardware)).
  A node on v2026.11.08-3 **refuses to update** to this release on a
  machine whose boot disk or network cards it couldn't drive - nothing
  switched, nothing rebooted; each node's log says what its devices
  are bound to at every boot (`hardware: boot disk vda: virtio_blk,
  virtio-pci; eth0: virtio_net, virtio-pci`). **Update a node of an
  older release to v2026.11.08-3 first**: the check runs in the
  release the node already has.
- **node_exporter's `nvme` collector is no longer offered**: it fails
  without NVMe. A node whose settings named it keeps the others
  ([the node exporter](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/metrics.md#the-node-exporter)).

## 🐧 Kernel

- **A kernel for KVM/QEMU virtual machines**
  ([#591](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/591)), on both tracks
  (Linux 7.3.3 stable, 6.18.62 longterm, the same versions as
  v2026.11.08-3). Gone: the physical network cards (tg3, bnxt, igb,
  ixgbe, i40e, igc, mlx5, r8169), VMware's vmxnet3 and pvscsi, NVMe,
  the RAID/SAS controllers, all of USB, PCI serial cards, IOMMUs,
  cpufreq, ACPI thermal/AC/battery/fan, Intel ME, vendor MCE, I2C.
  Kept: virtio, e1000/e1000e, AHCI, PIIX, SCSI disk and CD-ROM,
  CPU and memory hot-plug, NUMA, the framebuffer console.

  | | stable 7.3.3 | longterm 6.18.62 |
  |---|---|---|
  | Kernel image | 7.07 → 5.36 MB | 6.87 → 5.19 MB |
  | Kernel CVEs of 2025 applying to the build | 442 → 356 | 443 → 352 |
  | Kernel CVEs of 2026 so far | 1090 → 940 | 1087 → 934 |

- **Each image says what its kernel drives** (`image.json`'s
  `kernel.flavor`, `virt`, and `kernel.drivers`): the update check of
  v2026.11.08-3 reads it (see the upgrade notes).

## 🖥️ Controller

- **A release isn't hidden by one of its files GitHub won't serve**
  ([#600](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/600)): the morning
  v2026.11.08-3 came out, GitHub's release downloads answered errors
  now and then while its API answered, and the Controller offered no
  update for some forty minutes - one file missing dropped the whole
  release list. Now a release's small files are read once; a release
  whose `security.json` doesn't come is offered without its 🔒 badge
  until it does (read again three minutes later); and the last list is
  kept for six hours while GitHub fails, instead of ten minutes.

## 🌐 The image factory

- **The builder page doesn't wait for GitHub**
  ([#599](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/599)): its download
  statistics asked GitHub for each release's catalog, and waited 20 to
  30 seconds while GitHub was failing; they wait 4 seconds at most now,
  the HAProxy and kernel figures completed once GitHub answers.
  Already live on janus.sw-servers.net.

## 🧪 Tests

- `qemu-baremetal-test` follows the kernel's flavor (virtio-scsi
  instead of NVMe, e1000 instead of igb); `qemu-selinux-test`'s USB
  hot-plug check runs on a kernel with USB only.
- The v2026.11.08-3 pre-release's lab campaign
  ([#598](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/598)): the Consul fix
  proven on the path that failed in v2026.11.08-2.
